disputes.title: Refund-twice race: lockForUpdate on OrderItem prevents collision but DOES the seed actually re-read released_qty after lock acquired?
disputes.evidence_dispute: L364-366 query: $orderItem = OrderItem::query()->where('id',$line->id)->lockForUpdate()->first(). This refetches the row inside the lock, so released_qty read at L375 and used at L410 is post-lock fresh. Two concurrent refund requests: request A acquires lock, reads released_qty=0, computes seed 'released:0:delta:1', writes movement, increments released_qty to 1, commits. Request B then acquires lock, refetches released_qty=1, computes seed 'released:1:delta:1', writes movement (different key). NO COLLISION.

disputes.title: What if refund is dispatched WITHOUT prior decrement? requireOriginalDecrement guard L106-108 — does the release path L380-440 also enforce?
disputes.evidence_dispute: Inside releaseForOrderInTransaction: L401-404 — $orderKey = $this->movementKey('order_created', $order, $row, null); if (! StockMovement::query()->where('idempotency_key', $orderKey)->exists()) { continue; }. This IS the original-decrement guard for the partial-refund release path. Without prior decrement, no release row written. SAFE.

disputes.title: Composition snapshot mutation: if composition_snapshot is overwritten POST-decrement, release uses NEW snapshot to recompute requirements → wrong addon released

If overwritten by malicious admin OR migration, release would use wrong addon list. RELIANT on NF525 invariant.
disputes.verdict: CONDITIONAL PASS — depends on NF525 invariant. PricingService is frozen-zone. This is defense-in-depth: NF525 invariant is the moat.
